newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai rubber quiet, Japan bids too low - traders.
newsitem.headline: Thai rubber quiet, Japan bids too low - traders.

text.p: Activities in the Thai rubber market were subdued as most major markets in the region were closed for the Moslem Eid Al-Adha holiday, trade sources said on Friday.
Volume was modest with some buying interest from Japan but no deals were actually done as bidding prices were seen as too low.

"Their bidding price was 106.50 U.S. cents a kg which is well below the indication prices. When I saw the bids, I thought they must be joking. Who will sell at that price?," said one trader based in the southern town of Hat Yai.
Thai benchmark RSS3 for June delivery was quoted at around 110.00-112.00 cents a kg FOB Bangkok.
Traders said sharp falls in Japanese rubber prices and stocks remained bearish factors in the market.

"Prices now are lower than those two years ago. Market ideas seemed to be that prices would drop further. But I think it should be steady or firm a little, especially for RSS3, on short-covering," said another trader.
"Supplies of Thai RSS3 were rather tight. I think buyers will have to raise bidding prices otherwise no one will sell to them," he said.
